correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the source definition and symmetry. On every product of two boundary edges the objective is jointly convex, so the sphere supremum reduces to \(36\) ordered vertex pairs. Exact facet partitioning yields only \(1\), \(1+m-m^2\), and \(1+2m-3m^2\) on open parameter cells; the last dominates on \(0\le m\le1/2\). The unit pair \(x=(1,1)\), \(y=(0,-1)\) attains it for every such \(m\). The bundled verifier independently reconstructs the finite branch partition with exact rational arithmetic.
risks: The finite verifier certifies the polyhedral branch step only; the infinite reduction is the analytic convexity argument in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The source introduces \(L'_Y\) to quantify departure from a generalized parallelogram identity and links it to Hilbert geometry and uniform nonsquareness. The affine-regular hexagon is a canonical non-Hilbert polyhedral plane, so its complete exact profile is a natural benchmark. The result also reveals a structural feature invisible at the balanced classical parameter: the global maximum is \(4/3\) at \(1/3\) and \(2/3\), while the balanced value is \(5/4\). The convex edge-product reduction is reusable for related polygonal norms.
risks: This is a canonical-space benchmark rather than a classification of all polygonal norms.
